title: Compatibility gating and region-aware graceful degradation for model deployments
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket proposes a pragmatic deployment orchestration that enforces model-variant compatibility gates, region-aware failover policies, and tiered-capacity degradation rules during rollouts (canary/A-B/shadow). The goal is to reduce customer-facing regressions from model binary or config mismatches while preserving availability across geographic and capacity tiers.

Background:
We currently support model variants and regional routing, but there is no first-class compatibility gate or explicit degradation policy that considers: model architecture differences (kv-cache layout), quantization mismatches, client-expected tokenization/behavior, and capacity tiers (dedicated vs hosted). Past incidents (runtime-1.18 incident post-rollout) showed subtle KV-cache incompatibility leading to elevated error rates for long-context chat sessions in eu-west-1.

Proposal highlights:
- Compatibility Gate: a lightweight, declarative compatibility matrix attached to a model variant manifest. The gate encodes required runtime features (kv-cache format, attention pattern capability, max-seq tested) and automated validators (unit harness/unit tests + quick smoke canary on shaded instances). Only variants that pass the gate are eligible for traffic split.
- Region-Aware Degradation Policy: routing policies may declare per-region fallback chains. Example: eu-west-1 -> eu-central-1 -> fallback-global on capacity shortfall or SLO breach. Fallbacks respect privacy/region restrictions and are blocked if the model variant is marked non-compliant for the target region (e.g., air-gapped model).
- Tiered Capacity Degradation: routes include capacity tiers (tier-1 reserved, tier-2 burst, tier-3 best-effort). During overload, requests are downgraded by policy (reduce token budget, route to smaller quantized variant, or surface informative throttling).
- Rollout orchestrator changes: extend current rollout engine to evaluate compatibility gates before starting A/B or canary, perform shadowing experiments for 48–72h if the variant touches critical paths, and attach automatic rollback hooks triggered by combined signals (error spike, latency regression, quality drift defined by eval set).

Routing DSL (proposal):
- route policy = { preferred_regions: [...], fallback_chain: [...], allowed_variants: [compatibility_labels], capacity_tiers: [{name, min_qps}] }
- variant manifest includes compatibility_labels and test_artifact_links

Auto-rollback heuristics (first-pass):
- Immediate rollback: 5xx increase > 3x baseline for >5m in canary window OR > 2.5x in production region for >3m.
- Quality rollback: automated eval on stored prompt-set shows >4% drop in top-1 metric for 60m window after smoothing.
- Latency rollback: p95 increase > 150% and absolute increase > 200ms for >10m.
Rollback actions include: revert traffic split, mark variant as quarantined, notify SRE and PM, and create a follow-up ticket with pre-filled incident template.

Observability and Signals:
- Extend Console dashboards to show compatibility gate status per variant, per-region capacity utilization, and aggregated rollback-trigger counts.
- Instrument shadow runs to capture diffs (tokens, logits divergence summary) and expose sample diffs to PM/reviewer.

Acceptance criteria:
- Compatibility manifest schema v1 implemented and stored with every model variant in model-catalog.
- Rollout engine refuses traffic split for variants failing the compatibility gate.
- Per-region fallback chains can be configured via Console and respected by the routing plane.
- Auto-rollback hooks implemented with the first-pass heuristics and tested in internal staging.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Conservative gating increases time-to-deploy for risky variants but prevents high-cost incidents and customer regressions.
- More aggressive shadowing provides better signal but increases infra cost; limit to initial N hours or use sampling rates to control spend.

proposal_steps: Define compatibility manifest schema and store with variant metadata
Add small, fast validators to runtime that run during pre-deploy smoke (tokenizer check, kv-cache parity test)
Extend rollout engine to consult compatibility gate before traffic changes
Expose per-region fallback chains in Console and ensure routing plane honors them
Implement auto-rollback hooks with initial heuristics and create runbooks
Add shadowing instrumentation and eval-set automation to measure quality drift
decisions: Use a declarative compatibility manifest instead of embedding heuristics in code to keep validation portable
Default shadowing window for new variants set to 48h (configurable per-project)
Cross-region fallbacks disabled by default for variants marked 'region_sensitive'
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Increased deploy latency — Mitigation: allow bypass for urgent patches with explicit approval
Risk: Infra cost from shadowing — Mitigation: sampling and timeboxed shadow windows
Risk: False-positive rollbacks due to noisy metrics — Mitigation: combine multiple signals and smoothing before actuation
acceptance_criteria: Schema v1 committed and migrations run for existing variants
Rollout engine blocks variants without compatibility pass in staging
Console shows fallback chain and the routing plane respects configured fallbacks
Auto-rollback triggers exercised in a synthetic canary test and verified end-to-end
